$comment: Sim Lab part metadata v1 (docs/SIM-LAB-PLAN.md B3a). Authored by hand for this project from the official LDraw geometry, measured with bw-sim/ldraw/ldraw-geometry.js; never copied from BrickLink Studio, LDCad or any other connectivity database (plan D4). LDraw frame and units (LDU, -y up). test/bw-sim-part-meta.test.mjs checks every connector against the part mesh. Masses are estimates to +-20% (no published per-part masses); motor torque is LEGO's published stall torque for the medium angular motor (18 Ncm) and speed is the SPIKE 3 velocity limit used by docs/SPIKE-ARENA.md.
$references: LDraw assemblies vendored only so the metadata test can check a connector against LDraw's own placement (39370c01: where the castor ball sits in its socket).

parts.$comment: The LDraw name is "Technic Axle 4 with Stop". The length is left out of name/nameDe because a standalone 4 in a name is a whole-number search term: "axle 4 with stop" would make searchPalette("achse 4") return two parts and break test/bw-sim-palette-ui.test.mjs ("axle 4" is 3705 alone). The part number 87083 still finds it.

parts.name: Technic gear 20 tooth double bevel
parts.$comment: Double bevel: it also meshes a parallel same-module gear as a spur, but the compiler has one gear.type per part and cannot model both. bevel is the honest choice here: it is what the part is named, and it is the only way the right-angle mesh (the distinctive double-bevel case) is compiled.

parts.name: Technic gear 12 tooth double bevel
parts.$comment: See 32269.dat: double bevel modelled as bevel (right-angle mesh); the parallel spur mesh is not representable.

parts.name: Technic gear 36 tooth double bevel
parts.$comment: See 32269.dat: double bevel modelled as bevel. Its rim has three LDraw axle holes and two round pin holes; the centre axle hole (c) is listed first so the gear-centre check finds it.
